translations.text: When Jesus had come down from the mountain, great crowds followed him; and so on.
Matthew, the blessed Evangelist, wrote in this gospel reading that "the Saviour went down from a mountain, and a great multitude followed him.
Then behold, a certain leper came and bowed down before the Saviour, saying thus: Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.
The Saviour stretched out his hand and touched him, and said: I will; be cleansed. Then at once his leprosy was wholly cleansed, and he was healed.
Then the Saviour said to him: Take care that you tell it to no one; but go to God's temple, and show yourself to the priest, and offer your gift, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
The teacher Haymo says in his commentary on this that the mountain from which the Saviour came down signified the kingdom of heaven, from which the Almighty Son of God came down
when he took on our nature and became incarnate as a human being, so that he might redeem mankind from the devil's power.
He was invisible and incapable of suffering in his own nature; then he became visible in our nature, and capable of suffering.
The great multitude that followed him signified the faithful Christians, who follow the Lord with the steps of their conduct.
Truly, we follow Christ's footsteps if we imitate his examples with good works.
"Then behold, a certain leper came and bowed down before the Saviour, saying thus: Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.
The Saviour stretched out his hand and touched him, and said: I will; be cleansed. Then at once his leprosy was wholly cleansed, and he was healed."
In this deed God's might is shown, and his humility.
The law of Moses forbade anyone to touch a leper, but the humble Christ would not despise him, though he was loathsome, and he also showed that he was Lord of the old law, and not its servant.
In his might he could have healed him with his word, without touching; but he showed that his touch is very healing to the faithful.
The leper was faithful when he said, "Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me." The Saviour answered, "I will; and be cleansed."
Truly, God's command is deed, just as the psalmist said, "He spoke it, and the creatures were made. He commanded, and they were created."
In the spiritual sense this leprous man signified all mankind, which was loathsomely leprous with various sins in the inner man;
but it turned to faith in Christ, and wisely understood that it could not receive the cleansing of the soul except through the Lord, who committed no sin, nor was any deceit found in his mouth.
Loathsome is the leper's body, with many sores and swellings and with various discolorations; but the inner man, that is, the soul, is much more hideous if it is seized by various vices.
We must rightly believe in Christ, that he can heal our souls of the stains of sin; and we must steadfastly ask that his will be done.
His hand signifies his might and his incarnation. Just as Christ healed the leper by the touch of his hand, so too he redeemed us from the sins of our souls by taking on our flesh;
just as the prophet Isaiah said, "Truly he himself took away our sicknesses, and he himself bore our sorrows."
When he forbade the healed leper to make it known to anyone, by that he gave us an example that we should not spread abroad our good deeds,
but we must shun vain boasting with our inmost heart, if we do some little thing for good.
Truly, if we do good for the sake of vainglory, we will be repaid with no other reward than the torment of hell; for vainglory is a capital sin.
The old law commanded that every leprous man should come to the priest, and the priest was to separate him from other people if he truly was leprous.

If he was not clearly leprous, he was then counted clean by the priest's judgement. If the priest judged him leprous, and God's power afterwards healed him, then he was to thank God for his cleansing with an offering.

So too must the one who is inwardly leprous with deadly sins come to God's priest, and reveal his secret to the spiritual physician, and, by his counsel and help, heal his soul's wounds by doing penance.
Some people think that it is enough for complete healing if they confess their sins with a contrite heart to God alone, and that they need not confess to any priest, if they cease from evil;
but if their belief were true, the Lord would not have sent the man whom he himself had healed to the priest with any offering.
For the same example he also sent Paul, whom he himself had spoken to from heaven, to the priest Ananias, saying, "Go into the city, and there you will be told what you must do."

The priest did not make the man leprous or free of leprosy. Instead he judged that the man should be cut off from the company of men if his leprosy was getting worse, or that he should live among men if his leprosy was getting better.

So must the spiritual priest do: he must correct God's people, and cut off and excommunicate from Christian people the one who is so leprous in wicked habits that he defiles others with his wickedness;
About this the apostle Paul said, "Put away the evil one from among you, so that one diseased sheep does not infect the whole flock."
If his leprosy is getting better, that is, if he turns away from evil and corrects his ways through the fear of God, he may live among Christian people until he is fully whole in his way of life.
The evangelist said that "After this the Lord went to a town called Capernaum.
Then a centurion came to him, pleading and saying, 'Lord, my servant lies at home bedridden and is in great distress.' The Lord answered him, 'I will come and heal him.'
Then the centurion answered and said, 'Lord, I am not worthy that you should come in under my roof; but speak your word, and my servant will be healed.
I am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, "Go," and he goes; to another, "Come," and he comes; to my servant, "Do this," and he does it.'
When the Saviour heard this, he was amazed, and said to the crowd following him, 'Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith among the people of Israel.
I tell you truly, that many will come from the east and from the west, and will rest with Abraham the patriarch, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
The children of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
Then the Saviour said again to the centurion, 'Go home, and let it be done for you just as you have believed.' And the servant was healed from that hour."
This centurion approached the Saviour not halfway but fully. He approached with great faith, and with true humility, and wisdom, and true love.
He had great faith when he said, "Lord, speak your word, and my servant will be well."
Truly he showed great humility when he said, "Lord, I am not worthy that you should come in under my roof."
He had great wisdom when he understood that Christ, who walked visibly in the body among men, is present everywhere through his divinity.
He was not without true love when he asked the Lord to heal his servant.
Many other people asked the Lord for things, some for their own healing, some for their children's, some for that of dear friends;
but this nobleman asked for his servant's healing with true love, because true love does not set anyone apart by kinship.
The Lord saw this nobleman's many virtues and said, "I will come and heal your servant."
John the Evangelist wrote that "A certain under-king came to Christ and asked him to go home with him and heal his son, because he lay at the point of death.
Then the Saviour said to the under-king, 'Go home; your son lives.'
He believed the Saviour's words and went home. Then his servants came to meet him and told him that his son was well.
Then he asked at what hour he had grown better. They said, "Yesterday, past midday, the fever left him."
Then the father realized that it was the hour in which the Saviour had said to him, "Go home; your son lives." The king then believed in God, and all his household."
The Lord would not, when invited, go in bodily form to the king's sick child, but healed him while absent, by his word; yet he was ready, uninvited, to go in bodily form with the centurion.

Everyone knows well that a king has greater power than any centurion, but the Almighty Son of God showed by that deed that we should not honour the powerful for their power, but for their human nature;
nor should we despise the poor for their poverty; rather we should honour God's image in them.
The humble Son of God was ready to visit the servant in person, and he healed the nobleman by a command;
Of this the prophet said, "The Lord on high looks upon the humble, and knows the proud from afar."

The Lord marvelled at the centurion's faith, not as though he had not known him before, he who knows all things; but he made the man's faith known to people by praising it, since it was wonderful to him.

Where did that faith come to the officer from, except from the grace of Christ, who afterwards praised him with these words? "Truly I say to you, I have not found such great faith in the nation of Israel."
This was not said of the patriarchs or prophets, but of the people then present, who were not yet of such great faith.
Mary and Martha were two sisters who believed very greatly in God: they said to Christ, "Lord, if you had been here, our brother would not have died."
This officer said to Christ, "Speak your word, and my servant will be healed. I am a man set under authority, having soldiers under me;
and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; to another, Come, and he comes; to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
How much more can you, who are Almighty God, accomplish by your command whatever you will!"
The Lord said, "I say to you in truth, that many will come from the east and from the west, and will rest with Abraham the patriarch, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

These words are pleasant to hear, and they greatly gladden our hearts: that many will come from the east of the world, and from the west, to the kingdom of heaven, and will reign with the patriarchs in everlasting joy.

By the two regions, east and west, are signified the four corners of the whole world, from which God's chosen ones of every nation will be gathered to the dwelling of the patriarchs and of all the saints.
By the east may be signified those who turn to God in youth; because in the east is the beginning of the day.
By the west are signified those who turn to God's service in old age, because the day ends in the west.
This following saying is very fearful: "The children of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
The children of the kingdom are the Jews, over whom God reigned through the old law; but they rejected Christ and despised his teaching;
and he will cast them into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Many rich men, however, thrive with God, if they are righteous and merciful.

The patriarch Abraham was a rich man, and David the great king, and Zacchaeus, who gave half his possessions to the poor, and with the other half repaid fourfold whatever he had previously taken wrongfully, single for single.
These rich men and those like them come, through good conversion, to the eternal kingdom, which will never fail them.
Those are called children of God who love him more than this world;
and those are called the children of the kingdom who plant the roots of their hearts in this present life more than in Christ: such will be cast into darkness.
The gospel says, "Into the outer darkness." The outer darkness is the blindness of the body outside. The inner darkness is the blindness of the mind within.
Whoever in this present life is blinded within, so that he has no understanding or care about God's commandments, will afterwards be blinded outwardly as well, and deprived of all light;
because before that he spent his life without remembering God. The wretched guilty ones suffer torment in eternal fire, and yet that dark fire gives them no light.
Worms tear their bodies with fiery teeth, just as Christ said in his gospel, "There their worm never dies, nor is their fire quenched."
There those who were joined together in wicked deeds during their lives will be brought together in one torment, so that murderers suffer together eternally in torments;
and adulterers with adulterers, the greedy with the greedy, robbers with robbers, perjurers with perjurers perish in that broad fire without any end.
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, because the eyes will run with tears in the great burning, and the teeth will chatter in turn in the severe cold.
If anyone has doubts about the general resurrection, let him understand this saying of the Lord: that there will be a true resurrection where there are weeping eyes and gnashing teeth.
The Lord said to the centurion, "Go home, and let it be done for you as you have believed"; and his servant was healed from that hour.
From this we should understand how greatly a Christian's own faith will benefit him, when another man's faith benefited so greatly. Truly, the bedridden man was healed through the centurion's faith.
Faith is the foremost of all virtues; without it no one can please God; and the righteous man lives by his faith.
Let us believe in the Holy Trinity and in the true Unity: that the Almighty Father, and his Son, who is his wisdom, and the Holy Spirit,
who is the love and will of them both, are three in persons and in names, and one God, ever abiding in one Godhead, without beginning or end. Amen.
